title: Disaster Relief Deferral Program Rules (Hardship Assistance Programs)
content:
The Disaster Relief Deferral of the Hardship Assistance Programs is for a borrower whose residence on the profile lies in a county covered by a FEMA major disaster declaration with Individual Assistance.

## Taking the request

The request records the declaration number exactly as published and the declaration date as the qualifying event date. A Disaster Relief Deferral request is taken only when the current date is no later than the declaration date plus the program's request window. The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the declaration date, and a request on the last day is in time. The declaration date relies both on what the borrower reports and on the published declaration.

| Declaration date (hypothetical, non-leap year) | Request window | Last day to request | Request on the last day | Request the day after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 January | 90 days | 10 April | taken | not taken |

## Evidence

A FEMA registration document must be on file before the deferral is applied; the borrower's word that they live in the affected area is not enough.

## Applying the deferral

The deferral is applied without an acceptance step for up to the program's maximum deferred installments, counted from the loan's next due date on the decision date even if that due date is already past due, and late and returned-payment fees assessed on or after the declaration's incident start are waived as disaster relief.

## A second declaration

A second disaster declaration is a separate qualifying event.

The declaration type required, the request window and the most installments deferred are given in the program schedules.
